text:
sanjay: quick sync — we need a clear, low-cardinality span naming + semantic attrs for LLM requests. routing, quotas, cache hits, token counts, and model provenance are all over the place in telemetry today. any strong opinions on names/prefixes + what we should never export?

emma: +1. my proposal: keep span names simple and stable, e.g. `llm.request` for the user-facing request span; create short subspan names for perf hotspots like `llm.tokenize`, `llm.model_infer`, `llm.kv_lookup`. attrs should use a `redwood.` prefix to avoid colliding with upstream semantic conventions. example payload (OTel attributes):
```json
{
  "redwood.request_id": "uuid-1234",
  "redwood.model.name": "mistral-8x",
  "redwood.model.revision": "2026-03-01",
  "redwood.model.variant": "int8-q4",
  "redwood.routing.policy": "latency-first",
  "redwood.quota.bucket": "svc_prod_standard",
  "redwood.cache.hit": false,
  "redwood.cache.key_sha256": "sha256:abcd...",
  "redwood.tokens.requested": 120,
  "redwood.tokens.generated": 64,
  "redwood.prompt.fingerprint": "sha256:prompt-hash",
  "redwood.sampling.rate": 0.01
}
```
Important: never put raw prompt text in span attrs. only store fingerprints / hashes.

lee: two quick questions — 1) cache key hash still high-cardinality across models/users? 2) how do we signal fallbacks (model substitution) inside spans so console rollups can show fallback %?

emma: good q. 1) cache key hash is high-card only if we index it. we should treat `redwood.cache.key_sha256` as a non-indexed string for debugging only; for metrics/dashboards use boolean `redwood.cache.hit` and a low-card `redwood.cache.shard` (e.g., 0-31 bucket) if you need distribution. 2) for fallbacks, add `redwood.model.effective` (the model actually served) and `redwood.model.requested` (what caller asked for). then dashboards can compute fallback_rate = count(effective != requested)/count(total).

benji: exporter/retention notes: we must aggressively filter high-card attrs before they hit long-term storage. suggested retention policy: routing=enterprise -> keep spans 90d with full metrics; routing=platinum/committed -> keep 30d; default keep 7d. also sample heavy models at 0.1-1% for raw spans but keep aggregated metrics at 100%. propose an exporter pipeline rule set: redact raw prompt, hash user ids, drop `cache.key_sha256` except in full-debug export.

infra-bot: otel-exporter config: staged deploy to canary; only the canary org gets full debug export.

sanjay: sounds good. next steps: emma to draft short RFC with the proposed attribute names + cardinality guidance; benji to write exporter filter rules (retention + redaction); lee to wire metric dimensions for fallback & cache-hit buckets. i'll add this into the telemetry board and put a short card for console panels: cache-hit rate, avg tokens/generated per model, fallback rate, per-routing SLOs. :thumbsup:

emma: putting a PR template in the RFC to remind folks: - do not add raw PII attributes - prefer hashed fingerprints - add @eng-platform review for cardinality check

lee: one more thing — we should reserve `redwood.internal.*` for infra-only attrs that never leave private telemetry. call that out in RFC.

benji: FYI I'll add retention mapping yaml in the exporter repo and a sample `exporter.filter` rule that drops high-card attrs for `prod` rank.

infra-bot: deploy success: otel-exporter/staging v2.3.1 -> canary (1850004388)

sanjay: thanks everyone — let's ship the RFC by EOD Friday and mark the console card as blocked until we have the attr set.

emma: ack. will circulate the RFC draft by tomorrow morning.

benji: ack. will sketch retention rules by EOD. :white_check_mark:
